subject: Learning Methods
title: Teaching With Questions, Not Answers
description: A short lesson to help you apply Teaching With Questions, Not Answers.

hook.text: The Socratic method survives 2,400 years later because asking questions teaches more deeply than giving answers.

buildup.text: When you ask a question, the listener's brain generates an answer. That generation activates deeper processing.

discovery.text: Good Socratic questions are open-ended: What would happen if? Why does this matter? How does this connect?

twist.text: Formulating good questions is harder than giving answers. The teacher who asks well has to understand the material.

climax.text: After studying, create five open-ended questions about the material. If you can do that, you truly understand it.

punchline.text: If you can write the questions, you own the material.

quiz.question: Why does asking questions teach more effectively than giving answers?
options: Students remember questions longer than statements
The listener's brain generates answers, activating deeper processing
Questions are shorter and easier to memorize
